findings.source_passage: I will add (since there is an æsthetics in all things), is much more handsome and becoming to the boat, than hemp.
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical '(since there is an æsthetics in all things)' is a signature Melvillean aside — the narrator's self-conscious aestheticizing of utilitarian objects. The draft drops the parenthetical entirely, removing the digressive philosophical voice that defines this chapter's register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the parenthetical: 'I will add (since there is an æsthetics in all things), much more handsome and becoming to the boat.'

findings.source_passage: Nor can any son of mortal woman, for the first time, seat himself amid those hempen intricacies, and while straining his utmost at the oar, bethink him that at any unknown instant the harpoon may be darted
findings.why_it_matters: The source's elaborate periodic construction ('Nor can any son of mortal woman… bethink him…') is a signature rhetorical shape. The draft collapses it into a relative clause ('No son of mortal woman first seated…'), losing the syntactic tension and the phrase 'straining his utmost at the oar' that anchors the physical terror.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the periodic construction and include 'straining his utmost at the oar' to preserve both rhythm and physical specificity.

findings.source_passage: Yet habit—strange thing! what cannot habit accomplish?—Gayer sallies, more merry mirth, better jokes, and brighter repartees, you never heard over your mahogany
findings.why_it_matters: The exclamatory digression 'what cannot habit accomplish?' and the full series 'Gayer sallies, more merry mirth, better jokes, and brighter repartees' are rhythmically and rhetorically distinctive; the draft drops 'what cannot habit accomplish?' and 'more merry mirth' and 'brighter repartees,' flattening the comic-ironic crescendo.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full rhetorical question and the complete series: 'Yet habit—strange thing! what cannot habit accomplish?—Gayer sallies, more merry mirth, better jokes, and brighter repartees, you never heard over your mahogany.'

findings.source_passage: for, indeed, the calm is but the wrapper and envelope of the storm; and contains it in itself, as the seemingly harmless rifle holds the fatal powder, and the ball, and the explosion
findings.why_it_matters: The rifle simile ('as the seemingly harmless rifle holds the fatal powder, and the ball, and the explosion') is a rhetorically precise parallel that clinches the terror-of-calm argument. The draft mentions 'wrapper and envelope' but omits the rifle image entirely, losing an interpretively significant analogical move.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the rifle simile after 'wrapper and envelope of the storm': 'as the seemingly harmless rifle holds the fatal powder, and the ball, and the explosion.'

summary: Four medium-severity voice-flattening findings — the dropped æsthetics parenthetical, the collapsed periodic sentence, the truncated habit-digression, and the excised rifle simile — together constitute three-or-more medium findings, triggering regeneration.
